# Basketball Video Analyzer

> Free, open-source basketball video analysis tool built by a coach, for coaches.

Basketball Video Analyzer is a desktop application for cutting, tagging, organizing, and exporting basketball game footage. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, works entirely offline, and costs nothing.

## Key Features

- **Video Cutting**: Mark the start and end of a clip with a keypress (Z and M by default, both rebindable), with frame-by-frame stepping and HH:MM:SS time search
- **Hierarchical Categories**: Build category trees for offense, defense, transitions, or any coaching system, and save them as presets to reuse across projects
- **Clip Library**: Browse clips as a thumbnail grid or as an editable table, with inline editing of title, categories and notes, multi-select for bulk actions, and a keep/cut/review status per clip
- **Player Tagging**: Tag clips with the players involved and filter the library by player
- **Court Positions**: Mark where on the floor a play happened
- **Stats Dashboard**: Clip counts and durations broken down by category, player, and quarter
- **Present Mode**: Play a filtered set of clips back to back for a team film session
- **Telestration**: Draw over paused video (arrows, circles, freehand) and replay the annotations
- **YouTube Import**: Pull game footage in from a YouTube URL
- **Export**: Cut clips out as MP4 organized into category folders, or export the clip list as CSV, JSON, or Sportscode-compatible timeline XML
- **Project Organization**: Keep footage separated by game, opponent, or practice session

## Languages

The interface ships in 11 languages: English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Greek, Lithuanian, Slovenian, Serbian, and Turkish. Switching language does not require a restart.

- Website: https://basketballvideoanalyzer.com

- Issues: https://github.com/kauredo/basketball-video-analyzer/issues

## Technical Details

- Built with Electron, React, and TypeScript; video processing uses FFmpeg
- Cross-platform: Windows, macOS (signed and notarized), Linux (.deb and .rpm)
- Free and open source under AGPL-3.0
- No subscriptions, no accounts, no data collection; clips and projects stay on your own machine
- Created by kauredo (https://github.com/kauredo)
